image_description: A hammerhead shark swimming in blue water, viewed from a frontal angle. The distinctive cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head) is clearly visible with eyes at the tips. The body is streamlined with visible pectoral fins and a dorsal fin. The ventral side appears lighter than the dorsal side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic wide, flat, T-shaped head structure unique to hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark circular structures consistent with eyes are visible at the very ends of the horizontal head extension.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While nostrils should be there, the resolution and lighting make it impossible to definitively identify small nostril openings distinct from skin texture or shadows on the underside of the cephalofoil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the hammer is visible and appears relatively straight/slightly curved, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The torso tapers smoothly towards the tail, exhibiting the typical fusiform shape of a shark.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the shark appears darker (grey/blue due to water filtering) while the underside is distinctly lighter/white, showing countershading.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution is insufficient to resolve microscopic dermal denticles; the skin appears smooth due to distance and water diffusion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent triangular fin is visible on the back, positioned correctly behind the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Large, wing-like fins are visible extending from the sides of the body, matching the triangular description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin is visible in the background; the upper lobe is clearly larger and more extended than the lower lobe, typical of pelagic sharks.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The white underbelly appears overly smooth and plastic-like, lacking the subtle micro-texture expected from real shark skin, even at this distance. It resembles a 3D render's diffuse map rather than biological tissue.

There is a uniform 'smudged' quality to the background rocks and the tip of the caudal fin that feels more like AI-generated noise reduction or diffusion blur than natural optical depth-of-field or motion blur.
The mouth slit is indistinct and seems to merge slightly with the surrounding jaw tissue without a clear, sharp boundary line typical of shark anatomy. It looks somewhat 'melted' into the face.
